products.label: Habitable Zone Gallery distances (Kane & Gelino 2012), after Kopparapu et al. (2013, 2014)
products.process: Draw the four distances as three flat rings around the star, the conservative zone and the optimistic zone's two extensions of it, on the plane the orbits of planets b and d are drawn in.
limitations: A calculation from the star's temperature and luminosity, not an observation; a planet inside it is not known to be habitable.
The Gallery calculates from 2,900 K and 0.00151 solar luminosities; the star's page shows 3,098 K.
Neither planet's orbital tilt is measured: both orbits, and the zone, are drawn in the star's equatorial plane, tilted 47 degrees to the line of sight.
The orbits' position angle on the sky is not measured, so the plane's turn about the line of sight is the convention the orbits are drawn with.
